title: Core Vocabulary: Education

topic_snapshot.description: Essential vocabulary, collocations, and phrasing to discuss academic systems, learning methods, and educational challenges in IELTS.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: The subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: The new national curriculum places a greater emphasis on science and technology.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A high-quality photograph of a diverse group of high school students studying together at a modern library table, surrounded by textbooks and laptops.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject or theoretical concept.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: Modern pedagogy often focuses on interactive and student-centered learning rather than rote memorization.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A dynamic shot of a passionate teacher explaining a concept at a whiteboard to an engaged class, bright lighting.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: A grant, especially one awarded to someone to enable them to study at university or college.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: She was awarded a full bursary to study engineering based on her outstanding academic record.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A close-up of a smiling student proudly holding a scholarship award certificate or an acceptance letter, professional portrait style.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: The inability to read or write.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: The government has launched a campaign to eradicate adult illiteracy in rural areas.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A poignant documentary-style photo of an adult learning to write for the first time, holding a pencil and tracing letters on paper.

key_vocabulary_bank.meaning: Pursued in addition to the normal course of study.
key_vocabulary_bank.example: Universities often look for candidates who participate in extracurricular activities like sports or debate clubs.
key_vocabulary_bank.image_prompt_fallback: A vibrant photograph of a school sports team playing football on a green field during sunset, emphasizing teamwork outside the classroom.

collocation_builder.meaning: To continue studying at a university or college level.
collocation_builder.example: Many high school graduates pursue higher education to improve their career prospects.

collocation_builder.meaning: To fail to keep pace with the academic progress expected.
collocation_builder.example: Students who miss classes frequently are likely to fall behind in their studies.

collocation_builder.meaning: To expand one's range of knowledge, interests, and experiences.
collocation_builder.example: Studying abroad is an excellent way to broaden your horizons and learn about different cultures.

collocation_builder.meaning: To fulfill the necessary standards or grades for a course.
collocation_builder.example: Applicants must meet strict academic requirements to be accepted into the medical program.

upgrade_section.example: Some critics argue that an over-reliance on rote memorization stifles critical thinking.
The government is offering incentives to encourage more young people to pursue tertiary education.
The success of the school is largely due to its team of highly qualified educators.

sentence_frames: One of the primary benefits of [Noun Phrase] is that it allows students to [Verb Phrase].
It is widely argued that [Subject] should prioritize [Noun Phrase] in order to [Verb Phrase].
Despite the advantages of [Noun Phrase], a significant drawback is that [Clause].

ielts_usage_examples.writing_example: In contemporary society, it is widely argued that schools should prioritize practical skills over theoretical knowledge. While I acknowledge the value of subjects like mathematics and literature, I firmly believe that equipping students with vocational skills is crucial for their future career prospects.
ielts_usage_examples.speaking_example: Well, back when I was in high school, the curriculum was quite rigid and heavily focused on rote memorization. Looking back, I think a more interactive pedagogy would have been beneficial in helping us grasp complex concepts more effectively.

common_mistakes: Using 'learn' instead of 'study'. (e.g., 'I learn biology at university' -> 'I study biology at university').
Confusing 'education' (the process) with 'background' (personal history). (e.g., 'My education is very poor' -> 'My educational background is quite limited').

quiz.question: Which of the following phrases best describes the inability to read or write?
quiz.explanation: 'Illiteracy' specifically refers to the inability to read or write. 'Rote memorization' is learning by repetition, 'pedagogy' is the method of teaching, and 'extracurricular' refers to activities outside the normal curriculum.
